obligations.summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor must take into account all relevant circumstances (nature, gravity, duration, responsibility, mitigation actions, cooperation, prior infringements, notification, and annual budget) when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and determining its amount on Union institutions, bodies, offices, and agencies.
Union institutions, bodies, offices, and agencies that fail to comply with the prohibition of AI practices under Article 5 are subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 1,500,000.

Union institutions, bodies, offices, and agencies that fail to comply with any requirements or obligations under this Regulation other than those in Article 5 are subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 750,000.
exceptions: Non-compliance covered by Article 5 is excluded from this fine tier and governed by the higher fine ceiling under Article 100(2).

obligations.summary: Before taking fine decisions, the European Data Protection Supervisor must give the subject Union institution, body, office, or agency the opportunity to be heard, base decisions only on elements on which parties have commented, and closely associate any complainants with the proceedings.

The European Data Protection Supervisor must fully respect the rights of defence of parties concerned, including entitling them to access the file, subject to protection of personal data and business secrets.
exceptions: Access to the file may be limited to protect the legitimate interest of individuals or undertakings regarding personal data or business secrets.

obligations.summary: Fines collected under this Article must contribute to the general budget of the Union and must not affect the effective operation of the fined Union institution, body, office, or agency.

The European Data Protection Supervisor must notify the Commission on an annual basis of the administrative fines imposed pursuant to this Article and of any litigation or judicial proceedings initiated.
